short_excerpts.text: Recurrent layers enable a transformer model to perform arbitrarily many computations before emitting a token.

short_excerpts.locator: Section 3.1, recurrence display; plain-text transcription of math
short_excerpts.text: e = P(x); s_i = R(e, s_(i-1)) for i in {1,...,r}; p = C(s_r). States s are in R^(n x h), where n is sequence length and h is hidden dimension.
After finishing all iterations, the coda block processes the last state and produces the probabilities of the next token.
Our core recurrent block R starts with an adapter matrix A: R^(2h) -> R^h mapping the concatenation of s_i and e into the hidden dimension h. [Math transcribed to ASCII.]

Also note that the distance to s* does not always decrease monotonically (e.g. for school); the model may also trace out complicated orbits in its latent trajectory while processing information. [Math transcribed to ASCII.]

inspection_findings: The same recurrent operator accepts the previous state and the fixed embedded input; the loop does not add sequence positions.
Prelude and coda are distinct from the shared recurrent core. The lesson explicitly presents a minimal schematic, not Huginn implementation parity.
Read the design motivation and Remark 3.1 as well as the equations: recurrent input reinjection is a design choice, not a claim that every possible loop model converges.
The source reports nonmonotonic and orbital latent trajectories; neither a shared operator nor repeated access to e guarantees convergence to a correct answer.
